To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

nanostructured multilayered materials with alternating hard and soft layers can be designed to have high hardness and low wear rate, and that their deformation mechanisms are highly dependent on the layer thickness and interface microstructure.

the hardness of the NMM increases with decreasing layer thickness, the wear rate of the NMM decreases with increasing hardness, and the wear mechanism of the NMM is strongly dependent on the layer thickness and interface structures
decreasing the layer thickness of Al/Ti NMs led to an increase in hardness and wear resistance, and the deformation mechanisms of the NMM depend on layer thickness.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development and characterization of nanostructured metallic multicomponent multilayers (MMMs) with a high hardness and wear resistance.
the tribological and mechanical behavior and deformation mechanisms of nanostructured multilayers.
the effect of layer thickness on the deformation mechanisms and tribological behavior of Al/Ti NMs.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Al/Ti system is a promising material system for tribological applications.
a combination of a high interface density, high interface energy, and a high interface strength is the key to a high hardness and wear resistance of NMMs.
, in the case of NMMs, hardness and wear behavior can be correlated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the wear rate of the Al/TI NMMs is mainly governed by the hardness of the subsurface region, and the hardness of the NMM is mainly determined by the thickness of the individual layers.

the hardness of the Al/TI NMMs is determined by the interface structure and the thickness of the individual layers, while the tribological behavior is determined by the hardness, layer thickness, and interface structure.

the hardness, wear resistance, and deformation mechanisms of the Al/TTi NMMs were strongly dependent on layer thickness and microstructure of the interfaces, which were determined by layer thickness, deposition conditions, and post deposition annealing.
The main takeaway from our work is that
nanostructuring of metallic materials can lead to significant improvements in their mechanical and tribological performance.
the mechanical and tribological performance of the Al/T Ti NMMs is determined by their microstructure and the deformation mechanisms of the NMM layers.
the wear rate of Al/Ti NMs is determined by the hardness, and the hardness of the material is determined by the interface structure.
